name: flow-tools
desc: Collect, send, process, and generate NetFlow data reports
why: A NetFlow collection and processing toolkit opens a real door into router traffic telemetry that few developers ever examine.

brief.what_it_is: flow-tools is a set of command-line programs for working with NetFlow data, the flow records that routers export about the traffic they forward. Per the package description it collects, sends, processes, and generates NetFlow reports. The bundled executables suggest the inputs are NetFlow export packets from network devices, received or read from files, and the outputs are flow data files, filtered or merged flow files, text reports, and RRD round-robin graph databases. I could not confirm these details from the homepage, so this paragraph is based on the package description and the executable names.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gave no problem statement or author framing. The package description only says it is for collecting, sending, processing, and generating NetFlow data reports.
brief.install_notes: Nothing beyond the package listing was verified. The listing names 24 executables: flow-capture, flow-cat, flow-dscan, flow-expire, flow-export, flow-fanout, flow-filter, flow-gen, flow-header, flow-import, flow-log2rrd, flow-mask, flow-merge, flow-nfilter, flow-print, flow-receive, flow-report, flow-rpt2rrd, flow-rptfmt, flow-send, flow-split, flow-stat, flow-tag, flow-xlate. The brew caveats field is empty.
brief.standout: The executable names suggest a Unix-style pipeline of small single-purpose tools, such as capture, filter, merge, split, stat, and report, that chain together. The scout note calls it a window into router traffic telemetry, but that is the scout's opinion, not something the homepage states.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage is a Google Code Archive page, which is read-only storage for a project that was hosted on Google Code. That suggests the original hosting is no longer active, but I saw no release date, last commit, or maintenance note, so I cannot say whether it is maintained, quiet, or abandoned.
brief.caveats: The homepage returned only Google Code Archive boilerplate and a notice that JavaScript is required. It contained no README, documentation, usage examples, or command lines, so I could not verify what the tools do beyond their names. No README was reachable through the homepage, and I did not guess other URLs. Platform support, licence, and build requirements are unknown.
fetch_log: https://code.google.com/archive/p/flow-tools/ - loaded, but returned only the Google Code Archive page shell and a JavaScript-required notice. No README or project documentation was present.
